The long-awaited Zelda sequel, The Legend of Zelda: A Link to the Past, also arrived for the Super NES.\nL187: ### 1993\nL188: \nL189: The Super FX Chip was announced: a breakthrough technology for home video systems. Other subsidiaries were also established in France, UK, Spain, Belgium and Australia.\nL192: ### 1994\nL193: \nL194: The Super Game Boy accessory was released, expanding the library of games that could now be played on the Super NES. Nintendo introduced the Rumble Pak, which enabled players to feel the realistic vibrations contained in the game.\nL209: ### 1998\nL210: \nL211: Nintendo introduced Game Boy Color and the innovative devices Game Boy Camera and Printer, bringing new life to the longest-running hit in the history of interactive entertainment. Game Boy Color systems were cased in two brand-new colours: purple and clear purple.\nL212: \nL213: The highly anticipated The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time for Nintendo 64 was released, setting new standards and breaking pre-order records for any videogame to date.\nL214: ### 1999\nL215: \nL216: Nintendo released Pokémon throughout Europe on 8 October.
